retained_failures.failure: Windows Python received the literal scripts/*.py path because shell wildcard expansion did not occur.
retained_failures.remediation: Enumerate scripts with PowerShell and compile each exact path; all scripts passed.

retained_failures.failure: PowerShell ConvertFrom-Json coerced the ISO timestamp to a locale-formatted DateTime before passing it to the builder.
retained_failures.remediation: Pass the manifest's immutable ISO timestamp without PowerShell date coercion; regenerated bytes matched exactly.

retained_failures.failure: Six generated text artifacts used Windows CRLF bytes that Git would normalize to LF, invalidating their working-tree SHA-256 bindings after checkout.
retained_failures.remediation: Require LF through .gitattributes and explicit generator newlines, rebuild every downstream receipt and bundle, and compare staged blobs before publication.

retained_failures.failure: Five previously approved JSON evidence and governing artifacts matched their recorded CRLF hashes locally but had LF-normalized Git blobs, so a clean checkout could not validate the approved bundle or contract.
retained_failures.remediation: Classify the five paths as exact-byte historical review evidence, stage their unchanged reviewed bytes without text normalization, and verify both the historical and current bundles and contracts against staged blobs.

retained_failures.failure: The validator required the checkout directory name to equal the project name, so a valid commit failed when cloned into a verification-specific folder.
retained_failures.remediation: Derive canonical project identity from the expected remote repository URL and rerun validation in a fresh clone.

limitations: Byte-for-byte reproducibility covers the lightweight M1 control artifacts only.
No full satellite products, preprocessing outputs, or scientific results exist yet.
